title: Suresh Raina's Son Rio Takes First Steps in Cricket
excerpt: The former India and CSK all-rounder shared photos of his six-year-old son in cricket gear, visiting a bat factory to choose his first bats.
body:
• Former India all-rounder Suresh Raina shared photos of his six-year-old son Rio in cricket gear, marking the beginning of his cricketing journey
  • Rio was photographed visiting a bat factory and choosing his equipment, with Raina calling it a shared experience between father and son
  • Raina made 322 international appearances for India and was the first Indian to score centuries in all three formats, with every century coming overseas

Former India and Chennai Super Kings all-rounder Suresh Raina announced on Sunday that his six-year-old son Rio has taken his first steps in cricket, sharing a compilation of photos on Instagram that show the youngster in full cricket gear and visiting a bat factory to pick his bats.

"Like father, like son! And so, our cricket journey begins, bud. I'm looking forward to experiencing the joy, excitement and innocence of the game all over again, this time through your eyes. Let's make some beautiful memories together."

Raina posted the update on his Instagram handle @sureshraina3 on August 31. The images show Rio — born on March 23, 2020 — donning pads and handling bats at a factory, a familiar rite of passage for young cricketers in India. The six-year-old appears to examine the equipment with the curiosity of a child discovering the game his father played at the highest level for over a decade.

A Decorated International Career

"Let's make some beautiful memories together." Raina posted the update on his Instagram handle @sureshraina3 on August 31."

Raina, now 39, represented India in 322 international appearances between 2005 and 2018, spanning 18 Tests, 226 ODIs, and 78 T20Is. He holds the distinction of being the first Indian to score centuries in all three formats of international cricket, with every one of those centuries coming on foreign soil.

In ODIs, Raina scored 5,615 runs at an average of 35.31, with five centuries and 36 half-centuries. His T20I record shows 1,605 runs in 78 matches at an average of 29.18, including one century and five half-centuries. Across 18 Tests, he accumulated 768 runs with a best score of 120.

A key figure in India's 2011 Cricket World Cup triumph and one of the most celebrated players in Indian Premier League history through his long association with Chennai Super Kings, Raina announced his retirement from international cricket on August 15, 2020 — the same day former captain MS Dhoni confirmed his own international retirement.

The Raina Family

Rio is Raina's second child with his wife Priyanka. The couple welcomed their daughter Gracia in 2016. When Rio was born in March 2020, Raina announced the news on social media with the words: "We are proud to welcome our son & Gracia's little brother — Rio Raina."

The latest post swaps a birth announcement for a cricketing one, capturing the moment a retired international athlete gets to experience the game again through his child's eyes. The photos show a simple family outing — a six-year-old in the early stages of discovering a sport — but for followers of Indian cricket, the images carry the weight of generational continuity.

No Pressure, Just the Game

No academies or formal training programs have been announced for Rio. At six years old, the focus remains on the joy of the sport rather than any competitive ambitions. Raina's caption emphasized experiencing "the innocence of the game all over again," signaling that the moment is about a father and son sharing the sport that defined his career, rather than any expectations of a cricketing future.

For fans of Indian cricket, the images of a former star's child picking up his first bat resonate with a tradition where the sport passes through generations. Whether Rio eventually follows his father into professional cricket remains far in the future. For now, the story is a six-year-old with brand-new bats, and a father ready to bowl to him.
